rationale: The v2 exchange was limited by an unproven two-sided payer, post-match bypass and integrated processors that already control physical execution. The v4 redesign follows the working evaluation's highest-value change: one licensed processor becomes the payer and distribution anchor, generator onboarding is tied to recurring offtake contracts, and continued permission to the stream record becomes the intended data-retention mechanism. Removing the transaction take rate and retaining physical risk with qualified operators changes the revenue and acquisition structure without claiming that processor demand, contract rights, adoption, margin or transport economics are proven.
